new_commodity_proposals.evidence: Searched by food, not by string, across all four namespaces as reported by the pre-resolve table: the only pork-chop concept priced is the generic `pork-chops` (7/7 stores, cheapest 2.52 at Sam's Club), and no boneless variant appears under any spelling or word-order flip. Boneless loin chops are a distinct retail cut at a distinct price class (typically $3.50-4.50/lb vs ~$2.50 bone-in) AND a distinct gram basis, since the bone-in id's per-lb price buys ~30% bone. Bridging them would publish both a wrong price and a wrong portion for the main protein of the dish. Same distinction the estate already holds between leg quarters and thighs. If the registrar judges `pork-chops` to be a boneless-inclusive generic rather than a bone-in id, alias is the correct verdict and I have no objection.

registrar_rulings.reason: Verified against all three namespaces, the feed, and the raw Sam's capture: the only priced chop id is pork-chops, and its live crown (Sam's item 17799324269, $2.52/lb) is literally 'Member's Mark Bone-In Pork Chops' - so the existing id is the bone-in purchase, not a boneless-inclusive generic. Boneless loin chops are the same food in a different form (different price class and ~30% different edible yield per lb), the exact split the estate already holds for boneless-skinless-chicken-thigh vs chicken-thighs and boneless-beef-short-ribs vs beef-short-ribs. SAME FOOD, DIFFERENT FORM -> new id in the recipe namespace (recipe-board-everyday + recipe-commodities). REQUIRED FOLLOW-UP EDITS via add-commodity-rule.ps1: (1) allowlist pair boneless-pork-chops|pork-chops in commodity-dupe-allowlist.json, reason 'bone-in vs boneless: different per-lb basis'; (2) new id's include must REQUIRE boneless AND pork AND chop (e.g. ^(?=.*\bboneless\b)(?=.*\bpork\b)(?=.*\bchops?\b)) and inherit pork-chops' full exclude list (breaded/stuffed/seasoned/marinated/cooked plus the beverage/baby/pet block) - 'stuffed' stays excluded even though the recipe is baked-STUFFED-pork-chops, because the recipe buys raw chops; (3) add \bboneless\b to pork-chops' excludes so the form-blind include can no longer crown a boneless product on the bone-in id. Separate vocabulary answer: 'boneless pork chops' needs its own ingredients.json row (DIFFERENT FORM of Pork Chops, per pre-resolve) - this ruling mints the id only, not the name.
